summary: Mount Eddy lookout, Shasta-Trinity NF: cupola house completed in 1912, replaced by a Plan 4A cabin in the 1920s; removed on an unknown date, foundation reported at the summit.

facts.design: Cupola lookout house (1912), later replaced by a California Region 5 Plan 4A cabin
facts.status_note: Removal date unknown; the register says a foundation still exists at the summit, and a hiker's trip report mentions remains of an old lookout tower

staffing.status: last dated staff record in these sources is 1931 (Matt Merchant)

access.note: Reached on foot. The Forest Service describes a side trip from the Pacific Crest Trail to the summit. No road to the summit is described in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Forest Service describes the Sisson-Callahan Trail east from the PCT to the uppermost Deadfall Lake, then a side trail to the summit.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

events.note: Cupola lookout house completed on the summit (register description); 1912 newspapers describe the station going up
Completed and staffed in 1912 (register); a 1912 paper names the federal lookout on the peak
Lookout discovered all eighteen thunderstorm-started fires that August, per a September 1912 paper
Lightning struck the station in August 1920 and knocked out the lookout; an October 1920 windstorm blew out its windows
Forest Service dug a shelter tunnel at the lookout station
September 1923 windstorm left the lookout house a practically total wreck; the lookout and his son spent the night in the tunnel
Lookout Matt Merchant located a sawmill fire 54 miles away near Oak Run

corrections.proposed: 1912 built as a cupola house; replaced by a Plan 4A cabin in the 1920s
corrections.why: The register's own description says the cupola house was completed and staffed in 1912, and 1912 newspapers describe the station going up. The 1920s date belongs to the replacement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register Built field says circa 1920s, but its description says the cupola was completed and staffed in 1912. Story uses 1912 for the first lookout and 1920s for the replacement.
Register gives 9,040 ft; Forest Service gives 9,025 ft. Story does not give a figure.
The 1920 lightning victim appears in the clippings as McClemmons, McClemmens and other spellings. Story uses McClemmons.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1920 built date comes from the register's Built field; its description gives a cupola completed in 1912, so the record should be corrected. Removal date is unknown in every source read. The hiker's remains and the register's foundation may or may not be the same ruin. The Oregon Hikers post is an undated personal trip report, used only for what remains. The Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of newspaper clippings; staffing after 1931 is not documented in these sources, so the story stops there.
